### page_1
[AmericanJournalofScience,Vol.320,February,2020,P.125–149,DOI10.2475/02.2020.02]
ACOMBINEDGEOCHRONOLOGICALANDPALEOMAGNETICSTUDY
ON(cid:2)1220MAMAFICDIKESINTHENORTHCHINACRATONAND
THEIMPLICATIONSFORTHEBREAKUPOFNUNAAND
ASSEMBLYOFRODINIA
JIKAIDING*,SHIHONGZHANG*,†,HANQINGZHAO*,HANBIAOXIAN*,
HAIYANLI*,TIANSHUIYANG*,HUAICHUNWU*,andWEIWANG**
ABSTRACT. A new combined geochronological and paleomagnetic study was car-
riedoutonthelateMesoproterozoicmaficdikesinthenortheasternandcentralNorth
ChinaCraton(NCC).Threedikesweredatedat1224.2(cid:2)5.1Ma,1219.9(cid:2)6.0Maand
1215.2 (cid:2) 7.7 Ma through use of the secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) zircon
datingmethodandonedikewasdatedat1219.1(cid:2)4.3MabyusingSIMSbaddeleyite
dating method, indicating that these dikes emplaced at (cid:2)1220 Ma. A total of 286
paleomagneticcoresampleswerecollectedfromseven(cid:2)1220Madikesandtheirhost
rocks, as well as two (cid:2)775 Ma dikes for field tests. All the samples were subjected to
stepwise thermal demagnetization. Rock magnetic experiments of representative
samplesdemonstratethatthedominantmagneticcarriersofthe(cid:2)1220Madikesare
single-domainandpseudo-singledomainmagnetitegrains.Twopaleomagneticcompo-
nentswereidentifiedfromthe(cid:2)1220Madikes.Thelowtemperaturecomponentisa
viscous magnetic remanence acquired in the recent geomagnetic field. The high
temperature component (HTC) was isolated between 500 and 580°C, which directs
east and down with moderate inclination. A paleomagnetic pole (11.3°N, 175.8°E,
A (cid:3)7.6°)wasdeterminedbyaveragingsevenvirtualgeomagneticpoles(VGPs),each
V 9 G 5 PcorrespondingtothemeanHTCdirectionofanindividualdike.The(cid:2)1220Ma
pole passed a baked-contact test and appeared to adequately average out secular
variation. It differs from any younger poles of the NCC, and is thus considered as a
reliable pole for the NCC. While our new results place the NCC at intermediate
paleolatitudes((cid:2)28.8°Nforsitelocatedat36.8°N,113.4°E)at(cid:2)1220Ma,thecoeval
high-quality poles in the global paleomagnetic database, however, indicate that the
AustraliancratonswerepositionednearthepoleandLaurentiawaslocatedaroundthe
Equator, depicting a dispersed paleogeographic pattern of the three continents at
(cid:2)1220 Ma. The updated paleomagnetic data together with geological evidence may
suggest that the NCC separated from northern Australia between (cid:2)1320 and (cid:2)1220
Ma,andlaterjoinednorthwesternLaurentiabetween(cid:2)1220and(cid:2)1110Ma.
Keywords: paleomagnetism, (cid:2)1220 Ma mafic dikes, North China Craton, Nuna,
Rodinia
introduction
Ithasbeenwidelyrecognizedthatthepasttwobillionyearshavewitnessedatleast
threesupercontinents,namedNuna(alsoColumbia,fornamediscussionseeinEvans,
2013; Meert and Santosh, 2017), Rodinia and Pangea from old to young. Episodic
amalgamation and dispersal of the supercontinents have profoundly influenced the
evolutionofEarth’ssystem(forexample,NanceandMurphy,2013;Nanceandothers,
2014). The late Mesoproterozoic–early Neoproterozoic (1300–900 Ma) is generally
regardedasthecriticaltimeofthebreakupofNunaandthesubsequentassemblyof
Rodinia(Liandothers,2008;Pisarevskyandothers,2014a;Evansandothers,2016b),
butthetransitionprocessbetweenthetwosupercontinentsremainslargelyunknown

126 J.Dingandothers—Acombinedgeochronologicalandpaleomagneticstudyon
(Zhang and others, 2012; Pisarevsky and others, 2014a, 2014b; Meert and Santosh,
2017). There are myriad inferences about the style and rate of plate motions during
theMesoproterozoicwhichremainenigmaticduetothepaucityofreliablepaleomag-
netic data (Li and others, 2008; Zhang and others, 2012; Evans, 2013; Meert, 2014;
Pisarevsky and others, 2014a, 2014b; Evans and others, 2016b; Meert and Santosh,
2017).
Recently, several (cid:2)1220 Ma mafic dikes were reported from the North China
Craton(NCC)(Pengandothers,2013;Xiang,ms,2014;Peng,2015;Wangandothers,
2015,2016).WecarriedoutacombinedpaleomagneticandSIMSU-Pbgeochronologi-
calstudyforsevenfreshdikes,andobtainedahigh-qualitypaleomagneticpoleforthe
NCC at (cid:2)1220 Ma. This pole together with coeval high-quality paleomagnetic data
from other continents and geological information allow us to present a paleogeo-
graphicmapat(cid:2)1220Ma,whichsuggestslarge-scaleplatemotionfromthebreakupof
NunatotheassemblyofRodinia.
geological background and sampling
Thesamplingtripswerecarriedoutinthreeregions,namedtheJianpingregion
(figs.1Band1C),theLulongregion(figs.1Band1D)inthenortheasternNCC,and
theLichengregioninthecentralNCC(figs.1Band1E).
IntheJianpingregion,three(cid:2)1230Mamaficdikeswerepreviouslyreported(fig.
1C; Wang and others, 2015). The dikes vertically or subvertically emplaced into the
Archean–Paleoproterozoic(Ar–Pt )gneissesandthe(cid:2)1.7Gaalkalineplutons(Wang
1
and others, 2013a, 2013b). They are generally (cid:2)20 to 50 m wide, more than (cid:2)5 km
longandNNE-trending(fig.1C).Lithologically,thedikesarediabaseorgabbro,with
the main mineral assemblage of plagioclase and clinopyroxene. They are mainly
alkaline in composition with ocean island basalt (OIB)-type geochemical features
(Wang and others, 2015). Among them, two dikes were dated at (cid:2)1230 Ma (fig. 1C;
dike JP01, 1229 (cid:3) 10 Ma, 1231 (cid:3) 16 Ma; dike JP03, 1229 (cid:3) 4 Ma; Wang and others,
2015) using LA-ICP-MS zircon dating method. In this study, 119 paleomagnetic
samples from these three dikes were collected. In addition, 18 samples of two sites
(14JP05,14JP13)fromthegneissichostrockswerecollectedforabaked-contacttest.
In order to obtain more accurate age for the sampled dikes, coarse-grained block
samples((cid:4)20kg)fromthedikeswerealsocollectedtoseparatezirconandbaddeleyite
grainsfortheU-Pbgeochronologicalanalyses.
IntheLulongregion,twogroupsofthePrecambrianmaficdikeswerereported.
They are different in age, trend, lithology and many geochemical features (fig. 1D;
Wang and others, 2016). The older dikes are N-S trending. They are gabbro in
lithology(figs.2Aand2B)andtholeiiticincomposition.Oneofthedikeswasdatedat
1236.4 (cid:3) 7.3 Ma (dike LL02, fig. 1D; baddeleyite, SIMS, Pb-Pb; Wang and others,
2016). The younger dikes are NEE-SWW trending. They are porphyritic diabase in
lithology (figs. 2C and 2D) and alkaline in composition with OIB-type geochemical
features.Oneofthedikeswasdatedat775(cid:3)5Ma(dikeLL04,fig.1D;zircon,SIMS;
Wangandothers,2016).Allthesedikesare(cid:2)5to30mwide,andverticallyintruded
intotheAr–Pt gneisses.Inthisstudy,84paleomagneticsampleswerecollectedfrom
1
three (cid:2)1236 Ma dikes (dikes LL02, LL01 and LL03, fig. 1D) and 30 samples were
collectedfromtwo(cid:2)775Madikes(dikesLL04andLL05,fig.1D).
IntheLichengregion,35paleomagneticsampleswerecollectedfroma30-meter-
wide diabase dike (LC01) in the location (cid:2)30 km north of the Licheng County (fig.
1E).ThedikeisNW-SEtrendingandsubverticallyintrudedtheArcheangneissesand
Paleoproterozoic strata, the Changzhougou and Chuanlinggou formations, which
slightlydiptothewestwithadipangleof(cid:2)5°.Apreviousstudyreporteda(cid:2)1220Ma
mafic dike in this region, but did not provide the exact location (Peng, 2015). To
constraintheageofthedike(LC01)fromwhichwecollectedpaleomagneticsamples,

geochronological experiments, analyses and results
MethodandAnalyticalProcedure
Using conventional density and magnetic separation techniques, zircon and
baddeleyitegrainswereseparatedinthemineralseparationlaboratoryoftheBureau
ofGeologyandMineralResources,Langfang,HebeiProvince.Threedikes(JP01,JP02
and JP03) yielded sufficient zircon grains and one dike (LC01) yielded sufficient
baddeleyitegrains.Themineralgrainstogetherwiththestandardzircon/baddeleyite
grains were mounted in the transparent epoxy. The mount was then polished to
expose the longitudinal section of the crystals. All grains were documented with
transmitted and reflected light micrographs, as well as cathodoluminescence (CL)
imagesorback-scatteredelectron(BSE)imagestorevealtheirinternalstructures.
Zircon U-Pb and baddeleyite Pb-Pb analyses were conducted on a Cameca IMS
1280-HR Large-radius ion microprobe at the Institute of Geology and Geophysics,
Chinese Academy of Sciences (IGGCAS) in Beijing, following the method of Li and
others(2009,2010).Theanalyticalionbeamsusedinthisstudyareabout20(cid:5)m(cid:6)30
(cid:5)minsize.ThemeasuredU-Th-Pbratiosandtheirabsoluteabundancesinthezircon
grainswerecalibratedagainstthestandardzirconPlešovice(Sla´maandothers,2008)
and 91500 (Wiedenbeck and others, 1995). The standard baddeleyite Phalaborwa
(Heaman, 2009) was used to calibrate the Pb/U ratio and U concentration in the
baddeleyitegrains.Uncertaintiesonindividualanalyseswerecitedatthe1(cid:7)level,and
the weighted mean ages are quoted with 95 percent confidence intervals. Data

ZirconU-PbGeochronology
Three gabbro dikes in the Jianping region were dated using SIMS U-Pb zircon
dating method. Most of the zircon grains are 70 to 120 (cid:5)m in length and some are
longerthan150(cid:5)m(figs.3A–3C).Thegrainsareeuhedraltosubhedralinmorphol-
ogyandtheyshowbandedorbroadzoningintheCLimages(figs.3A–3C),whichare
thetypicalfeaturesofmagmaticzirconsfromgabbroanddiabase(Corfuandothers,
2003).
SampleD15JP01wascollectedfromdikeJP01.Thirty-twospots,onespotoneach
zircon grain, were analyzed. Some high U ((cid:4)3000 ppm) grains were not used for
furthercalculation(tableA1).UandThconcentrationsoftheremainingzirconsvary
from394to2893ppmand261to4857ppm,respectively,withTh/Uratiosof0.66to
1.77 (table A1). Twenty-five of these analyses are concordant and define a concordia
age of 1224.2 (cid:3) 5.1 Ma (95% confidence, MSWD (cid:8) 1.8), being identical to the
weighted mean 207Pb/206Pb age of 1226.9 (cid:3) 3.4 Ma (95% confidence, MSWD (cid:8) 1.9;
fig.4A).The207Pb/206PbdatesareconsistentwithpreviousLA-ICP-MSzirconresults
withintheiruncertainties(1231(cid:3)16Ma;1231(cid:3)10Ma;Wangandothers,2015).We
interpretedthenewconcordiaageof1224.2(cid:3)5.1Maasthecrystallizationageofdike
JP01.

paleomagnetic experiments, analyses and results
LaboratoryConditionsandProcedures
Eachpaleomagneticsamplewascutinto1to3standardcylindricalspecimensof
2.5cmindiameterand2.2cminheight.Onespecimenofeachsamplewassubjected
tostepwisethermaldemagnetization,andrepresentativespecimensweresubjectedto
rockmagneticanalyses.Stepwisethermaldemagnetizationwasconductedinintervals
of3to50°Cupto580°CusingaTD-48furnace,whoseinternalresidualfieldislower
than 10 nT. Remanence was measured on a JR-6A spinner magnetometer and a 2G
755-4Ksuperconductingmagnetometer.Thefurnaceandmagnetometersarehoused
inamagneticallyshieldedroomwithamagneticfieldbelow(cid:2)300nT.Temperature-
dependent low field susceptibility in an argon atmosphere was conducted using a
KLY-4S Kappabridge equipped with the CS-3 high-temperature apparatus. These
experiments were finished in the Paleomagnetism and Environmental Magnetism
Laboratory at the China University of Geosciences, Beijing (CUGB). Hysteresis loops
and back-field demagnetization of saturation isothermal remanent magnetization
(IRM) were conducted using a MicroMag Model 3900 Vibrating Sample Magnetom-
eter at the Institute of Geophysics, China Earthquake Administration. Remanence
components were processed using the principal component analysis (Kirschvink,
1980), and the mean directions were calculated using Fisher statistics (Fisher, 1953).
Paleomagnetic data were analyzed using the program packages developed by Enkin
(ms, 1990) and Cogne´ (2003). Paleocontinent reconstructions were made using the
GPlatesfreewarepackage(Williamsandothers,2012).
RockMagneticResults
To identify the magnetic carriers, rock magnetic experiments were conducted on
representative specimens of the (cid:2)1220 Ma dikes from the three regions. Temperature-
dependentlowfieldmagneticsusceptibilitycurvesshowtheCurietemperatureof(cid:2)580°C
and the pronounced Hopkinson peak in the heating curve (fig. 5A), indicating the
presence of PSD or SD magnetite in the specimens (Dunlop and Özdemir, 1997).
Hysteresis loops and back-field demagnetization of IRM show most specimens are satu-
ratedbelow500mTwithcoercivitieslessthan(cid:2)30mT(figs.5B–5D).OntheDaydiagram
(Dayandothers,1977;Dunlop,2002),mosthysteresisdatafallinthePSDgrainsizearea
(fig. 5E). In summary, the rock magnetic results demonstrate that the main magnetic
carriersinthesespecimensarePSDandSDmagnetitegrains.
PaleomagneticResultsoftheDikes
Afterstepwisethermaldemagnetization,mostsamplesfromtheseven(cid:2)1220Ma
dikesinthethreeregionsrevealedconsistentresults.TheNRMintensitiesrangefrom
0.1to4.0A/m.Mostspecimensarecharacterizedbytwowell-definedcomponents.A
lowtemperaturecomponent(LTC)wasisolatedbelow300to400°C(figs.6A–6G).Its
directions coincide with the geocentric axial dipole (GAD) field (figs. 7A–7G). It is
thus interpreted as a viscous remanent magnetization (VRM) of the recent geomag-
netic field. After removing the LTC, a high temperature component (HTC) was

with a dip angle of 5°, we applied tilt correction to its HTC and obtained the
tilt-correcteddirection(D(cid:8)89.3°,I(cid:8)50.9°,k(cid:8)154.5,(cid:9) (cid:8)2.2°;table1).

The corresponding virtual geomagnetic pole (VGP) of the HTC of each indi-
vidualdikewascalculatedandlistedinthetable1.ByaveragingthesevenVGPsfrom
the three regions (table 1; fig. 8J), we got a mean paleomagnetic pole of 11.3°N,
175.8°E(A (cid:8)7.6°)fortheNCCat(cid:2)1220Ma(fig.8J;NC1220,table2).
95
Mostspecimensofthetwo(cid:2)775MadikesfromtheLulongregionalsoyieldedtwo
components: an LTC defined below 400 °C and an HTC defined between 500 and
580°C.TheLTCofdikeLL05directsaroundthelocalGADfield(fig.7I)andwasthus
interpretedasaVRMofrecentgeomagneticfield,whiletheLTCofdikeLL04shows
scattereddirections(fig.7H).TheHTCsofthetwodikesconsistentlydirectENEwith
shallow inclinations (figs. 8G–8H; table 1), and differ significantly from those of the
(cid:2)1220 Ma dikes (figs. 8A–8F, 8I). The different HTCs observed from the (cid:2)1220 Ma
and (cid:2)775 Ma dikes in the same sampling area may exclude any regional pervasive
remagnetization event after (cid:2)775 Ma. Due to the limited sampling of the (cid:2)775 Ma
dikes, the corresponding VGPs are unlikely to be enough to average out the secular

EvaluationofPalaeosecularVariations
Paleomagneticdatafromasingledikerepresentsonlyaspotreadingofthegeomag-
neticfield(Tauxe,1993),soitisimportanttoevaluatewhetherourdatahaveaveragedout
thepalaeosecularvariations(PSVs).Inthisstudy,twomethodswereappliedtoascertain
whethertheresultshavesufficientlywell-sampledPSV.Thefirstmethodiscomparingthe
angulardispersion(S)ofVGPsofasamplesetwithPSVmodels(Bigginandothers,2008;
Smirnovandothers,2011;VeikkolainenandPesonen,2014).TheSofVGPswascalculated
using the method of Biggin and others (2008), and the confidence interval (1(cid:7)) was
calculatedusingthen(cid:10)1jackknifemethod(Efron,1982).TheSofthesevenVGPsis9.7°,
witha95percentconfidenceintervalof(8.0°,11.4°).Thisresulthasanoverlapwiththe

### page_15
(cid:2)1220MamaficdikesintheNorthChinaCratonandtheimplicationsforthebreakup139
expectedvalue(10.2°,15.2°)forpaleolatitudeof28.8°(referencepoint:36.8°N,113.4°E)
accordingtothePSVmodelfor1.0to2.2Ga(Smirnovandothers,2011).Whileitisalittle
smallerthantheexpectedvalue(11.4°,13.7°)accordingtothePSVmodelfor0.5to1.5Ga
(Veikkolainen and Pesonen, 2014). These comparable results indicate the secular varia-
tion appears to have averaged out. The other method is the N-dependent A envelope
95
(Deenenandothers,2014),whichboundedanupperlimitA andalowerlimitA
95max 95min
toevaluatewhetherornotadistributionhassufficientlywell-sampledPSV(Deenenand
others,2014).TheA ofourpoleis7.6°,whichiswithintheA envelope(A (cid:8)5.5°,
95 95 95min
A (cid:8)24.1°),suggestingthePSVcouldhaveaveraged.Insummary,the(cid:2)1220Mapole
95max
oftheNCC(poleNC1220,table2)wereportherehasapositivebaked-contacttest,has
averagedoutsecularvariationanddoesnotresembleanyyoungerpolesfromtheNCC.
Accordingly, the pole is given a Q-score (Van der Voo, 1990) of 6 because of lacking
reversals.
discussion
Intheglobalpaleomagneticdatabase,therearetwohigh-quality(cid:2)1220Mapoles
fromothercratons.OnewasobtainedfromtheGnowangerup-FraserdikesofAustralia
(pole GN, table 2). The pole passed a baked-contact test and a reversal test and was
dated at 1218 to 1203 Ma using SHRIMP U-Pb zircon and baddeleyite method
(Pisarevsky and others, 2014b and references therein). The other pole was obtained
from the Sudbury dikes of Laurentia (pole SuD, table 2; Palmer and others, 1977),
which was dated at 1235 (cid:11)7/(cid:10)3 Ma (Baddeleyite, TIMS, Pb-Pb; Duda´s and others,
1994), and the pole passed a baked-contact test. The three poles (NC1220, GN and
SuD listed in table 2) can be regarded as reliable poles to constrain the paleogeo-
graphicpositionsofthesepaleocontinents.
Therearealsoseverallessreliableandproblematicpolesthatneedbriefdiscussions:
(1)ThepaleomagneticpoleobtainedfromtheYunmengshanFormationoftheRuyang
Group in the southern margin of the NCC passed a fold test and a reversal test. It was
regarded as a high-quality pole of (cid:2)1260 Ma (Zhang and others, 2006). Recently, ages
obtainedfromthetuffbedsintheLuoyukouFormation(1611(cid:3)8Ma,1634(cid:3)10Ma,
1638(cid:3)9Ma;zirconU-PbLA-MC-ICPMS)inthewesternHenanProvince(Suandothers,
2012;Liandothers,2017),however,suggestthatthepolesobtainedfromtheLuoyuand
Ruyanggroupsintheregion(Zhangandothers,2000,2006),whichoncewereconsidered
asof1.3to0.8Ga,shouldbeof(cid:2)1.78to1.61Ga.(2)Apolewasobtainedfromtheigneous
rocksoftheNovaFlorestaFormationintheAmazoniaCraton.Althoughtherockshave
well-determined age ((cid:2)1200 Ma, 40Ar-39Ar, biotite; Tohver and others, 2002), the pole
doesnotholdanypositivefieldtesttosupporttheinterpretationofitsprimaryorigin.(3)
The pole was obtained from the Late Kibaran intrusions of Congo (Meert and others,
1994).Itsagewasoriginallyplacedat1236(cid:3)24Ma(Meertandothers,1994),butrecent
workindicatesthepolemaybe(cid:2)100millionyearsolderthanitwasestimated(Maierand
others, 2007; Tack and others, 2010). (4) The pole was obtained from the Harohalli
alkalinedikesofIndia.Thepaleomagneticdatahaddualpolaritywhichfailedreversaltest
(Radhakrishna and Mathew, 1996; Pradhan and others, 2008). It could average out the
PSV based on the N-dependent A envelope method (Deenen and others, 2014) or
95
comparingtheSofVGPswithPSVmodels(Smirnovandothers,2011;Veikkolainenand
Pesonen,2014).Butthelackofconvincingfieldtestsmakesthispolelessreliable.These
problematicpolesmentionedabovewillnotbefurtherconsideredinthepaleogeographic
reconstructionsinthisstudy.
The three reliable poles of (cid:2)1220 Ma listed in the table 2 (poles GN, SuD and
NC1220)placetheAustraliancratonsinthenear-poleregion(fig.10A;Pisarevskyand
others, 2014b), Laurentia in the equatorial region with its present western margin
facingnorth(table2;fig.10A;Palmerandothers,1977;Duda´sandothers,1994),and
theNCCinthemoderatepaleolatitudeswithitspresentnorthernmarginfacingwest

Fig.10.PaleogeographicreconstructionsoftheNCC,Australiancratons,Laurentia,BalticaandSiberia
(consistsofAldanandAnabar)at(cid:2)1450Ma,(cid:2)1220Maand(cid:2)930Ma.Continentsandtheirpolesarematched
in color. Paleopoles used are listed in the table 2. (A) (cid:2)1220 Ma reconstruction. The Australian cratons,
LaurentiaandNCC(NCC1–5)arereconstructedbasedontheir(cid:2)1220Mapoles“GN”,“SuD”and“NC1220”,
respectively.Baltica-LaurentiaconnectionfollowsthatinNuna(Cawoodandothers,2010)asshownin(B).The
long-lived“tightconnection”modelofSiberiaandLaurentia(Ernstandothers,2016;Evansandothers,2016a)
wasadoptedinallthreereconstructions.ThedashedoutlinesoftheNCCshowthedifferentoptionsbecauseof
thefromdomofpaleolongitude.(B)(cid:2)1450Mareconstruction(modifiedafterZhangandothers,2012),and
paleomagneticpoles(“SF”and“MA”intable2)wereusedtoplotthepaleolatitudeofthesupercontinent.(C)
(cid:2)930Mareconstruction(modifiedafterZhaoandothers,2019).Balticaisreconstructedaccordingtoits(cid:2)940
Mapole“B940”,LaurentiaisrotatedtoBalticaaccordingtothe“right-way-up”model(CawoodandPisarevsky,
2006),andtheNCCisrotatedtoBalticabymatchingtheirearlyNeoproterozicpoles(Fuandothers,2015).Euler
rotationparametersarelistedintableA3.MC,MawsonCraton;NAC,NorthAustralianCraton;SAC,South
AustralianCraton;WAC,WestAustralianCraton.
(fig.10A),respectively.Comparingthethreecontinents’paleogeographicpositionsat
(cid:2)1220 Ma with those in Nuna at (cid:2)1450 Ma reveals three obvious changes: (1) the
NCC-northernAustraliaconnectioninNuna(fig.10B;forexample,Zhangandothers,
2012; Pisarevsky and others, 2014a) was not viable at (cid:2)1220 Ma (fig. 10A); (2) the
Australia-Laurentia connection in Nuna (fig. 10B) supported by the Paleo–Mesopro-
terozoic paleomagnetic and geological data (Zhang and others, 2012; Pisarevsky and
others,2014a;Nordsvanandothers,2018;Pourteauandothers,2018)wasnotviableat
(cid:2)1220Ma,whilethetwocratonswereseparatedbyalargelatitudinalgapat(cid:2)1220Ma
(fig. 10A; Pisarevsky and others, 2014b); (3) from (cid:2)1450 to (cid:2)1220 Ma, Laurentia
experienceda(cid:2)30°counterclockwiserotation(figs.10Aand10B),whereastheNCC
experiencedlittlerotation,indicatingtheirindependentplatemotionbetween(cid:2)1450
and(cid:2)1220Ma.ThesechangescollectivelyindicatethatNunahadbrokenupby(cid:2)1220
Ma,althoughtheglobalpaleomagneticdatabasecannotconstrainmorepreciselyyet
whenNunabrokeupbetween(cid:2)1400and(cid:2)1220Ma.

### page_17
(cid:2)1220MamaficdikesintheNorthChinaCratonandtheimplicationsforthebreakup141
Itmaybeworthtomentionthat,duetothepolarityuncertainty,theNCCcouldbe
alternativelyplacedinthesouthernhemisphere.Ifthat,thedistinctmovementrelativeto
othercontinentscanalsodemonstratethatsupercontinentNunahadbrokenupby(cid:2)1220
Ma. Combined with NCC’s position in the Nuna models (Zhang and others, 2012;
Pisarevsky and others, 2014a; Meert and Santosh, 2017), given the paleolongitudinal
freedomallowed,thepositionofNCC2(NCC1–5infig.10A)couldbethefinalchoiceto
minimizeitsrelativemovementsfrom(cid:2)1450to(cid:2)1220Ma(figs.10Aand10B).
Several studies seem to have reached a consensus that a long-lived connection
betweentheNCCandnorthernAustraliamightexistbetween(cid:2)1780and(cid:2)1320Ma(for
example, Zhang and others, 2012, 2017; Kirscher and others, 2018; Wang and others,
2019).Majorlinesofevidenceincludethepaleomagneticconsistency(Zhangandothers,
2012;Kirscherandothers,2018),thesimilaritiesofthe(cid:2)1320Malargeigneousprovinces
(LIPs) and sedimentary successions (Zhang and others, 2017), as well as some deposits
(Wangandothers,2019)preservedintheYanliaoriftbasinoftheNCCandtheMcArthur
basinofthenorthernAustralia.Ifthelong-livedconnectionreallyexisted,theNCCdid
separatefromthenorthernAustralialikelybetween(cid:2)1320and(cid:2)1220Ma(fig.10A).
The new (cid:2)1220 Ma paleomagnetic results provide important constraints for the
formationofRodiniaandtherelationshipbetweentheNCCandLaurentia.Arecent
reconstruction placed the NCC along the present northwestern margin of Laurentia
from (cid:2)1110 to 890 Ma based on paleomagnetic data and detrital zircon provenance
analyses(fig.10C;Fuandothers,2015;Zhaoandothers,2019),whichmeanstheNCC
joined the NW Laurentia and the Yenisei side of the Siberian Craton (see the
discussioninZhaoandothers,2019),by(cid:2)1110Ma.TheNCCwouldrequireatleasta
(cid:2)60°counterclockwiserotationrelativetoLaurentiaduring(cid:2)1220and(cid:2)1110Mato
closethespatialgapbetweentheNCCandNWLaurentia.Geologicalevidenceofthis
convergence process, however, has not been found yet, which could be attributed to
the poorly understanding of the three regions: the northern margin of the NCC,
western margin of the Siberian Craton and NW Laurentia. Our analyses predict that
there were considerable geological records that were associated with the breakup of
Nuna and assembly of Rodinia in these regions had been dispersed or intensively
superimposedbylatertectonicactivitiesthatneedstobeverified.
conclusions
Three new SIMS U-Pb zircon ages and one SIMS Pb-Pb baddeleyite age confirm
thatthe(cid:2)1220Mamaficdikesdevelopedwidelyinthenortheasternandcentralparts
of the NCC. A new paleomagnetic pole (11.3°N, 175.8°E, A (cid:8) 7.6°) was obtained
95
from seven (cid:2)1220 Ma mafic dikes. The pole passed a positive baked-contact test and
appearedtoaverageoutsecularvariations.ItplacestheNCCinamoderatepaleolatitu-
dinalregionat1220Ma,whilethecoevaldatafromLaurentiaandAustraliaindicatea
dispersedpaleogeographicrelationshipbetweentheNCCandthosetwocratons.The
updated paleomagnetic database together with the geological evidence suggest that
theNCCseparatedfromthenorthernAustralialikelybetween(cid:2)1320and(cid:2)1220Ma
andjoinedtheNWLaurentiabetween(cid:2)1220and(cid:2)1110Ma.
